import { defineTable, col } from "@rebasepro/server/schema";

// ⚠ Not reproduced exactly by `rebase db push` — read before pushing:
//   - "type" is a varchar with no length, declared as text: a push would convert it to text, which keeps every value.
//   - "recipient_type" is a varchar with no length, declared as text: a push would convert it to text, which keeps every value.
//   - "read_at" is timestamp without time zone, declared with `col.custom()`: Rebase serves it as the driver returns it, and `rebase db generate` / `db push` refuse it until the planner can plan a custom type (`custom-sql-type`).
//   - "seen_at" is timestamp without time zone, declared with `col.custom()`: Rebase serves it as the driver returns it, and `rebase db generate` / `db push` refuse it until the planner can plan a custom type (`custom-sql-type`).
//   - "created_at" is timestamp without time zone, declared with `col.custom()`: Rebase serves it as the driver returns it, and `rebase db generate` / `db push` refuse it until the planner can plan a custom type (`custom-sql-type`).
//   - "updated_at" is timestamp without time zone, declared with `col.custom()`: Rebase serves it as the driver returns it, and `rebase db generate` / `db push` refuse it until the planner can plan a custom type (`custom-sql-type`).
export const noticedNotifications = defineTable("noticed_notifications", {
    columns: {
        id: col.bigserial().primaryKey(),
        type: col.text(),
        eventId: col.bigint().notNull(),
        recipientType: col.text().notNull(),
        recipientId: col.bigint().notNull(),
        readAt: col.custom("timestamp without time zone"),
        seenAt: col.custom("timestamp without time zone"),
        createdAt: col.custom("timestamp without time zone").notNull(),
        updatedAt: col.custom("timestamp without time zone").notNull()
    },
    rls: "admin-only"
});
